title: A Study of PORT-77 for the Treatment of erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) or X-linked protoporphyria (XLP)
official: A Phase 2b/3, Quadruple-Blinded, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Study of PORT-77 Administered Orally to Adults and Adolescents with Erythropoietic Protoporphyria or X-Linked Protoporphyria and an Open-Label Extension
summary:
Main objective: Part 1 
_To characterize the dose-response of PORT-77 on plasma PPIX levels compared to placebo 
_To evaluate the safety and tolerability of each dose of PORT77  
Part 2 
_To evaluate the efficacy of PORT-77 to decrease PPIX levels compared with placebo 
_To evaluate the efficacy of PORT-77 on average daily time in sunlight without pain compared with placebo 
_To evaluate the safety and tolerability of PORT77   
Part 3 
_To evaluate the long-term efficacy of PORT-77 to decrease PPIX levels 
_To evaluate the long term safety and tolerability of PORT-77
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1_Aged 12 years or older
2. 2_Clinical history of EPP, XLP or EPP2 supported by one of the following: -	Genetic confirmation of EPP -	Genetic confirmation of XLP  -	Genetic confirmation of EPP2 -	Elevated total RBC PPIX >3 × ULN, elevated metal free PPIX and/or elevated ZnPPIX levels in RBCs consistent with EPP/XLP/EPP2 based on historical laboratory test results
3. 3_Has symptoms of EPP/XLP, history of consistent, non-painful prodrome within approximately 45 minutes of sunlight  exposure and prior to phototoxic attacks, desire to increase time spent in sunlight but currently limited by symptoms of EPP/XLP
4. 4_Body weight or BMI at screening as follows: _For participants aged 12 to <18 years: body weight≥32Kg _For participants aged≥18 years: BMI≥18.5Kg/m2
5. 5_AST and ALT <3xULN and total bilirubin <2xULN  (unless documented Gilbert syndrome) at screening
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1_Diagnosis of another porphyria or another  photodermatosis that may confound the evaluation of PORT-77
2. 10_Clinically significant  cardiac dysfunction
3. 2_Any evidence of clinically significant organ dysfunction or any clinically  significant deviation from normal in the clinical or laboratory assessments, per the Investigator’s discretion
4. 3_Major surgery within 8 weeks before Screening or  incomplete recovery from any previous surgery
5. 4_History of, or anticipated need for, liver transplantation  or history of bone marrow transplantation
6. 5_Active infection with hepatitis B or C
7. 6_History of drug or alcohol abuse  within the last 12 months prior to screening
8. 7_Has taken any medication, vitamin, or supplement that alters sensitivity to  light exposure within 90 days of Day 1, or has taken bitopertin within 120 days of Day 1, or has taken iron within 30 days of Day 1
9. 8_Current or planned use of any of the following from 30 days prior to the first dose and throughout the study: _Drugs, herbal remedies, or foods/beverages (ie, grapefruit, Seville orange, star fruit) known to be strong or moderate inhibitors or inducers of CYP3A4 enzymes - Drugs with a narrow therapeutic window known to be sensitive substrates of the CYP3A4 enzyme _Drugs or herbal remedies known to be inhibitors pf P-gp or ABCG2/BCRP _Systemic hormonal contraceptives (with the exception of LNG-IUS) _Systemic estrogen (ie, hormone-replacement therapy)
10. 9_hypersensitivity to  PORT-77 or excipients
